keyPoints.line: set by the state, the same statewide.

read.bigIdea: In Michigan, spirits come through the state.
read.where: Michigan is a **control state** for spirits. The **Michigan Liquor Control Commission** sets a **uniform price** for each spirit, and on-premises licensees like us buy at a **discount** off that price. The Commission appoints **Authorized Distribution Agents (ADAs)** to warehouse and deliver spirits; an ADA never **owns** them. Beer and wine come through licensed **wholesalers**.
read.stopsTitle: From the still to our shelf
read.mixup: An **ADA** delivers spirits but doesn’t set the price or own the bottle. The **state** sets the price.

keyPoints.line: knows the brand: use them to learn.
is ours: buy for the menu.

read.bigIdea: A rep is a partner, not the buyer.
read.where: Brand **reps** and **wholesaler** reps bring samples, training and news of what’s coming. Use them: a good rep can **teach** the team a spirit. But the **list is ours**: buy what fits the menu and sells, not what’s pushed. Get anything promised (a staff training, a delivery date) **in writing**.
read.mixup: A free sample isn’t a reason to put a bottle on the list. **Sales** and the **menu** are.

keyPoints.line: you get what’s released, not what you want.
a menu never depends on one.
them with care: a story, not a markup.

read.bigIdea: Limited bottles are allocated, not ordered.
read.where: Some bottles are **limited**. You don’t order them like the well: you get what’s **allocated** to the bar, often a few bottles, sometimes none. So **never** build a menu drink on an allocated bottle. Feature them as **specials** and pours, sell them with their **story**, and track every pour.

stops.name: Feature
stops.text: A **special** or a pour, not a menu staple.

read.mixup: An allocated bottle on the cocktail menu is a drink you’ll **86** in a week.

keyPoints.line: name one in the spec book.

read.bigIdea: Spec only what you can always get.
read.where: Before a bottle goes into a menu spec, check it’s in **steady supply** through our suppliers (in Michigan, spirits through the state’s system). Note a **backup** bottle in the spec book in case it runs out. **Cost** the drink with the real bottle before the menu prints.
read.mixup: A bottle you found once isn’t a menu bottle. **Steady supply** is.

sources: Michigan Liquor Control Code, MCL 436.1205 and 436.1233 (legislature.michigan.gov/documents/mcl/pdf/mcl-Act-58-of-1998.pdf); House practice (ours; GM to confirm). Written for Mise in our own words, Nov 12, 2026.
